beliefs: The box reverses the order of characters in the input string [E1]
Whitespace characters (spaces, tabs, newlines, and all Unicode whitespace) are removed from the output rather than preserved [E2, E5, E8]
After reversing, all whitespace is stripped, so 'a b' -> 'ba' and ' lead' -> 'dael' [E2]
Case, digits, symbols, and non-whitespace invisible/format characters (ZWJ, ZWNJ, BOM, soft hyphen, word joiner) are preserved as-is, only order changes and whitespace is dropped [E1, E9]
Reversal is by Unicode code point, so astral characters and combining marks stay intact as units [E6, E7, E10]
Lone surrogates and unpaired UTF-16 code units are reversed as individual code points without error or alteration [E11, E12]
A surrogate pair split by whitespace is NOT recombined: the two halves reverse as separate code points, so '\ud83d \ude00' -> '\ude00\ud83d' [E13, E14]
Two adjacent lone surrogates that form a valid pair are treated as a single astral character when reversing [E17]
Whitespace between a lone high and lone low surrogate is removed but the halves are never merged into an astral character [E18, E19]
The box reverses first, then strips whitespace, so whitespace removal never causes new surrogate pairs to merge [E19]

When reversing, adjacent code units that form a valid surrogate pair are grouped as one unit, but a high surrogate followed by whitespace is not paired with a low surrogate across that whitespace [E13, E17, E20]

The reversal operates on the original string's code-unit units (grouping only originally-adjacent valid pairs), then whitespace is stripped from the reversed result; this matches all surrogate observations including E21 [E11, E13, E14, E17-E21]
notes: E21's observed outputs match v8 exactly; the 0.90 'match' is a per-string artifact of the harness comparing surrogate-containing strings, not a real discrepancy. No rule change needed, but I added a clarifying belief summarizing the reverse-then-strip order for surrogates.
